## Active Venezuela in 12 Days: Roraima, Rivers, and Angel Falls

The main goal of this journey is to climb [Mount Roraima](/venezuela/place/mount-roraima/) on foot, explore its rocky plateau, descend to the savanna, and then travel to [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). The name “Jurassic Water World” is figurative: there is no conventional water park with slides here. Instead, you travel amid real rivers, canyons, rainforests, table mountains, and waterfalls.

**Duration: 12 days and 11 nights.** Of the three Venezuela routes compared here, this one demands the most physical preparation. The [“Colors of Venezuela” tour](/venezuela/tour/colors-of-venezuela/) also includes Angel Falls but does not involve a multi-day climb up Roraima. Travelers who only want to see a tepui from afar can choose a less demanding format; this journey centers on the ascent and life in trekking camps.

## How the Physical Effort Is Distributed

| Days | Main Stage |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Caracas, journey toward Roraima |
| 3–7 | Trekking, plateau, descent |
| 8 | Transfer to Puerto Ordaz |
| 9–10 | Carrao River and Angel Falls |
| 11–12 | Caracas, departure |

After arriving in [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/), participants continue with a domestic flight and transfers according to the itinerary. The following day is devoted to a long journey to [San Francisco de Yuruani](/venezuela/place/san-francisco-de-yuruani/) and preparations for the mountain section. This is a good opportunity to check your backpack, boots, rain gear, and which personal belongings you will carry into camp.

On day three, after reaching the trailhead, travelers walk through savanna and river areas toward the Pemón settlement of Paraitepui, then cross the Tek and Kukenán rivers. In rainy months, water can be high, and crossings require additional safety measures, sometimes including a rope. These crossings are a serious reason to assess the trip against your real fitness rather than striking photographs of the plateau.

## The Ascent, Camping, and a Day on the Summit

Day four is the climb to the plateau. The trail passes through wet forest, streams, rocky stretches, and the “Two Tears” waterfall. Conditions change with the weather: water flow may increase, making the stones slippery. On the summit, the group camps in tents beneath a rock overhang. Day five is reserved for walks among rock formations, small pools, quartz, mosses, and plateau vegetation.

Tepui table mountains are interesting for more than their appearance. UNESCO describes them as geologically and biologically distinctive Canaima massifs with sheer cliffs and endemic species. On Roraima, this is evident in the details: wet stone, unusual surface shapes, limited shelter from wind, and changing clouds. In poor visibility, a panorama may disappear into mist, but the plateau's geology remains a reason to visit.

Day six is dedicated to descending toward the Tek River, and day seven to returning to the start of the route and driving back to San Francisco de Yuruani. This is not a five-day walk with a hotel return every evening: the group sleeps in tents and spends several days away from everyday comforts.

## From Roraima to Angel Falls: The Logistics

Day eight is spent on the journey to [Puerto Ordaz](/venezuela/place/puerto-ordaz/), approximately 8 hours according to the itinerary. On day nine, a charter flight takes travelers to Canaima National Park. The journey continues in traditional motorized curiara boats along the Carrao River, toward Raton Island, with **an overnight stay in hammocks**. The following day includes a hike to the Angel Falls viewpoint, the return to Canaima Lagoon, a passage near Sapo Falls, and a visit to a Pemón village.

Read the financial terms carefully: **the Puerto Ordaz–Canaima charter flight is paid separately and excluded from the base services**, although other domestic flights are included. Entry to Canaima National Park is also a separate expense, **$40 per person**. These details matter more than a vague statement that “all flights and transfers are included,” which would be inaccurate for this tour.

Day eleven brings the group back to Caracas; day twelve is reserved for city sightseeing and departure. The lengthy nature section leaves little free city time.

## What Is Included, and What Costs Extra?

Included are accommodation along the itinerary in hotels, posadas, camps, tents, and hammocks; scheduled transport and transfers; meals as specified for each day; excursions; English-speaking guides for most of the journey; and a Russian-speaking guide in Caracas. Separately listed expenses include medical insurance, tips, optional excursions, porter services on Roraima, a single-person tent, a mattress, and a sleeping bag. Some of these items can be discussed as rentals where specified.

A Russian-speaking guide **throughout the entire journey** is not part of the base services. On a demanding trek, understanding instructions about river crossings, camps, and safety is especially important. If your group requires another language, arrange it before selecting dates and paying.

Ask the organizer how much equipment each traveler carries, how meals work in the camps, who decides on weather-related changes, and how much time is allowed for the long transfer before the charter. These practical questions follow directly from the program and matter for fitness and budgeting.

## Who Is This Journey For?

The tour suits travelers interested in **several consecutive days of hiking** and overnight stays in wilderness camps. It also includes riverboats, possible heavy rain, and early departures. If you are unsure of your health, stamina, or trekking experience, discuss the actual stages with the organizer and consult an appropriate doctor if you have medical restrictions.

Those seeking a broader introduction to Venezuela without climbing Roraima can consider [“New Conquistadors”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/), a journey with more geographical variety, beaches, the Los Llanos plains, and Andean regions.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Trekking on Roraima

### Do You Have to Complete the Whole Route on Foot?

The mountain section involves several days of trekking, ascending, exploring the plateau, and descending. Transport takes the group to the trailhead, but does not replace the walking stages on Roraima.

### Are There Overnight Stays in Ordinary Hotels?

Part of the journey uses hotels and posadas, but the ascent involves tents, and the river stage in Canaima includes a night in hammocks. This is an important aspect of the accommodation.

### Is the Puerto Ordaz–Canaima Charter Included?

No. It is expressly listed as a separate flight outside the base price. Other domestic flights are included.

### Does the Route Guarantee Clear Weather on the Plateau?

No. Mist and heavy rain are possible, while river crossings depend on water levels. The daily plan must take account of the decisions made by local guides.

### Is This the Best Choice If I Only Want to See Angel Falls?

Probably not: a substantial part of the 12 days is devoted to Roraima. For a shorter introduction to [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), compare the six-day “Colors of Venezuela” program.

## Canaima and Margarita in 12 Days: How the Journey Works

The [Venezuela tour with a Margarita Island beach stay](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) combines three different holiday experiences: discovering [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/), boat and hiking excursions in [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), and several days on [Margarita Island](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/). It suits travelers who want to see Angel Falls and then relax by the Caribbean Sea without a multi-day mountain trek.

The itinerary's defining feature is that **free days matter as much as sightseeing days**. Days 2–3 in Caracas are left for independent exploration or additional programs. After Canaima, days 8–11 are dedicated to relaxing on Margarita, with an optional island sightseeing excursion. That preserves a substantial beach holiday after an eventful journey to the waterfalls.

## What Happens in Caracas and Canaima?

On arrival in Caracas, a meet-and-greet, transfer, and accommodation are scheduled. Optional outings from the capital include city sightseeing, Colonia Tovar, and an introduction to Santa Teresa rum production. These are choices for free days, so it would be wrong to present them all as included excursions.

Day four features a flight to Canaima. The program includes a boat excursion on [Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/place/canaima-lagoon/) and visits to waterfalls, including [Hacha](/venezuela/place/hacha-falls/) and [Sapo](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/). Walking behind the curtain of water at Sapo depends on conditions and local guides' instructions.

Day five is devoted to Salto Ángel. Travelers follow the Carrao River in motorized curiara boats, then walk through forest to a viewpoint. This is **a full, active day**, not a brief stop at the waterfall: expect an early departure, a river section, a forest trail, and a return toward evening. Grippy footwear, rain protection, and a change of clothing are important.

Water levels and weather affect access to Angel Falls. The itinerary explicitly allows the one-day visit to be replaced by a **two-day, one-night option sleeping in hammocks** if river levels are too low. Such a change must be coordinated before confirming the route and subsequent flights.

## Why Is There a Free Day in Canaima?

Day six allows travelers to recover after the boat journey and forest walk. Optional programs include a flight over Angel Falls, Kavac Canyon, a trek on Kuravaina, lagoons, and other outings. They differ in duration, transport, and participation conditions.

**A list of optional excursions is not a list of included services.** Weather may affect flights, while boat and hiking routes require separate confirmation. If you prefer to keep only the core nature experiences, you can spend the day quietly at the camp beside the lagoon.

## The Beach Stay on Margarita Island

Day seven connects Canaima and [Margarita](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/): a flight via Caracas, meeting, and a hotel transfer are scheduled. Accommodation is offered at Sunsol Ecoland on an all-inclusive basis. The next four days are dedicated to the sea.

Distinguish **the meal plan at the island hotel** from meals during the other stages. “All-inclusive” applies to Margarita accommodation; it does not promise the same service in Caracas, at the Canaima camp, or on a long river excursion. Alcohol and additional drinks are separately listed among the exclusions.

Travelers who prefer more natural regions and frequent movement can compare another [12-day Venezuela tour featuring contrasting landscapes](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/). On the Margarita itinerary, by contrast, much of the second week is spent on one island.

## What Is Included, and What Needs Separate Arrangements?

The package includes accommodation, transfers, domestic flights, scheduled excursions, meals, and a Russian-speaking guide. International flights, insurance, the Canaima National Park fee, tips, and optional excursions are excluded. This distinction matters from day one: your international arrival needs to fit the scheduled transfer.

When arranging the trip, Ada Tours helps coordinate domestic flight connections, free days, optional excursions, and the possibility of an overnight stay if the approach to Angel Falls changes. Pay particular attention to the Canaima–Caracas–Margarita connection and departure from the island: time spent flying is not beach time.

If a long hike across a rocky plateau is your main priority, compare this journey with [Mount Roraima trekking](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-mount-roraima-trek-12-days/). On the Margarita trip, the most physically demanding nature day is the Angel Falls excursion; the pace then becomes much gentler.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Canaima–Margarita Tour

### How Many Days Are Available for Relaxation on Margarita?

Days 8–11 are fully dedicated to island relaxation; day seven is for flying and hotel check-in. An optional Margarita excursion can be added, but is not mandatory.

### Is There a Hike to Angel Falls?

The described one-day program includes a forest trail to the viewpoint after the boat section. You need suitable shoes and readiness for wet weather.

### Are All Canaima Excursions Included?

No. Core sightseeing days and optional activities are listed separately. Flights, Kavac, and other optional outings must be agreed with their prices and feasibility in mind.

### Is This Itinerary Suitable for Someone Without Trekking Experience?

There is no multi-day Roraima ascent, but the Angel Falls excursion does involve physical activity. Consider the boat section, travel time, and forest walk. If you need an entirely relaxed itinerary, discuss possible changes with the organizer.

## Canaima and Angel Falls in Four Days: What a Short Itinerary Offers

The [four-day Canaima tour](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/) focuses on one natural region of Venezuela. It includes three nights in a lodge, round-trip flights from Caracas, excursions around the lagoon, and a full day of boat travel and hiking to Angel Falls. This is for travelers who want to dedicate several days to the national park without continuing to the islands or taking a multi-day Roraima trek.

Canaima National Park lies in southeastern Venezuela and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its tepui table mountains and waterfalls occupy vast natural spaces where **getting to the attraction is part of the experience**. Even a short tour depends on river transport and weather conditions.

## What Happens on Each of the Four Days?

| Day | Main Activities |
|---|---|
| 1 | Flight, lagoon, Sapo and Hacha |
| 2 | Carrao and Churún rivers, Angel Falls |
| 3 | Free time and optional excursions |
| 4 | Return to Caracas |

**Day one** begins with a flight from Caracas to Canaima, check-in, and lunch by [Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/place/canaima-lagoon/). Then comes a boat trip to [Sapo](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/) and [Hacha](/venezuela/place/hacha-falls/) waterfalls. These are distinct natural sites, quite different from Angel Falls much farther away.

**Day two** is the most demanding. After an early transfer to the dock, travelers follow the Carrao and Churún rivers, then walk toward Angel Falls. The trip takes a full day, includes lunch, and returns to Canaima. Water levels and weather may change access and the sequence of travel.

**Day three** is for relaxing by the lagoon, walking, or enjoying the included kayaking. Separate optional outings are also offered: flights to Kavac Canyon and Angel Falls, a trip to Pozo Azul, trekking on Kuravaina, Yuri and Yurilu waterfalls, and a helicopter excursion. **These additional activities cost extra.**

**Day four** includes breakfast and the return flight to Caracas. Departure time is approximate; the current schedule is confirmed when booking. Leave a buffer for international connections so that the journey back from a remote park does not depend on an exceptionally short transfer.

## Tapuy Lodge or Waku Lodge: What Must You Choose?

The itinerary offers two accommodation options, Tapuy Lodge and Waku Lodge. Both are part of the three-night journey but have different rates. Day two explicitly mentions Waku Lodge, so before confirming the booking, clarify whether the same daily description applies to your chosen accommodation option.

Agree on the lodge, room type, number of guests, language of guiding, and full inclusions before paying. **A hotel named on a particular day is not an automatic promise that you will stay there** when booking the other rate.

The package includes round-trip Caracas–Canaima flights, ground transfers in Canaima, guides and local staff, accommodation, meals according to the daily program, excursions to Angel Falls and the lagoon waterfalls, kayaking, and daily light snacks. The park entry fee, alcoholic drinks, tips, and optional excursions are excluded.

## Who Is This Itinerary For?

Choose four days in Canaima when waterfalls and river scenery are your main priorities and you have only a few days available. Be prepared, however, for boats, wet weather, and a hike on the Angel Falls day.

If you want Caribbean beach relaxation after Canaima, compare the [Margarita Island tour](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/). If you prefer a multi-day mountain hike with tents and an exploration of a quartz-rich plateau, explore the [Mount Roraima itinerary](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-mount-roraima-trek-12-days/). These involve different experiences and require more time.

Access to waterfalls, flights, and trails in Canaima depends on weather. Ada Tours helps coordinate the order of excursions, connections, and your chosen lodge; exact arrangements are confirmed for each journey.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Four Days in Canaima

### Can I See Angel Falls in Four Days?

Yes. The published program reserves a separate full day for Angel Falls. The actual river route depends on water levels and weather.

### Is There a Free Day?

Yes. Day three is left for resting by the lagoon or optional activities; kayaking is listed among the included services.

### Are Flights from Caracas Included?

Yes, Caracas–Canaima–Caracas airline tickets are part of the package. International arrivals and subsequent travel are planned separately.

### Are All Flights Over Angel Falls Included?

No. Helicopter and airplane excursions are optional activities on day three and cost extra.

## “Colors of Venezuela” in Six Days: Caracas, Canaima, and Angel Falls

This compact journey suits travelers who want to explore [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) without spending several weeks moving around Venezuela. The itinerary focuses on [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/) and Canaima National Park: a capital sightseeing tour, the waterfall-lined lagoon, a river excursion to Angel Falls, and two days when you choose your own pace.

**Duration: 6 days and 5 nights.** The defining feature is four consecutive days in Canaima after the opening day in the capital. Unlike the [12-day Roraima expedition](/venezuela/tour/active-venezuela-jurassic-water-world/), this journey has no multi-day camping trek. Nevertheless, the Angel Falls day still requires an early start, a boat trip, and a walk through tropical forest.

## How the Six Days Are Organized

| Day | Main Activities |
|---|---|
| 1 | Caracas and sightseeing |
| 2 | Canaima, lagoon, Sapo |
| 3 | Boat trip and walk to Angel Falls |
| 4–5 | Free time by the lagoon |
| 6 | Flight to Caracas |

After being met at the airport by a Russian-speaking guide, day one focuses on the capital. The description mentions the National Pantheon, Plaza Bolívar, historic buildings, and memorial sites associated with Venezuela's independence. Accommodation is at Eurobuilding Hotel Suites Caracas, in a Deluxe Standard room. Some city stops depend on arrival time, and a visit to Ávila is optional.

Day two includes a Caracas–Canaima flight, accommodation at Waku Lodge, a curiara boat trip around the lagoon, a walk on Anatolia Island, and passage **behind a curtain of water** at El Sapo Falls. Several waterfalls flow into the lagoon, including Hacha, Ucaima, Golondrina, and Wadaima, all mentioned in the itinerary.

## A Full Day at Salto Ángel

Day three is the journey's main nature experience. The boat sets off early along the Carrao River toward Auyán-tepui. The route continues through Devil's Canyon toward Raton Island, where a forest hike begins. According to the itinerary, the group reaches a viewpoint opposite Angel Falls after approximately one hour of walking.

Angel Falls plunges from the edge of an immense tepui in Canaima National Park. UNESCO recognizes this region for its exceptional landscapes of table mountains, cliffs, waterfalls, and distinctive plateau ecosystems. Views depend on clouds and water flow; identical clear skies and the same photograph seen in promotional material cannot be promised for every date.

The excursion lasts approximately **05:00 to 18:00**. It includes boats, a hiking route, a short trek through jungle, and a return to camp. Grippy footwear, spare clothes, and rain protection are needed. Swimming at the base of the waterfall is mentioned as a possible extra offered by local guides, not a guaranteed part of the day.

## Why Are Two Free Days Included?

Days four and five take place beside Canaima Lagoon. You can relax or choose additional activities: a helicopter or airplane flight over Angel Falls, an outing to Kavac Canyon, trekking on Kuravaina Tepui, a visit to the Blue Lagoon, a cycling trip to Sakaika Lagoon, kayaking, or paddleboarding.

This is **a menu of optional experiences**, not a promise to do everything in two days. Flights are subject to aviation and weather conditions, while hiking and water activities depend on route accessibility. Before paying, prioritize one or two activities and check the actual timetable. If your main aim is to see Angel Falls from above, discuss how a weather window could fit with your return flight.

Some extras have their own prices: **a helicopter flight $600 per person**, **an airplane flight over Angel Falls $320**, **a Kavac Canyon option $520**, **Kuravaina trekking $150**, **the Blue Lagoon $90**, and **a cycling excursion to Sakaika $80**. These are prices for **different separate activities**, not mandatory components of a package, and are not automatically added together. No fixed rate is provided here for paddleboarding or kayaking.

## What Is Included?

The package includes accommodation at the named hotels, private transfers and excursions in Caracas, group transfers and excursions in Canaima, meals according to the itinerary, and **domestic Caracas–Canaima–Caracas flights**. The guide in Caracas speaks Russian; guides in Canaima speak English. Consider this distinction when selecting a group, particularly if you need detailed translation of nature and safety briefings.

Optional excursions, the **$40 Canaima National Park entry fee payable locally**, medical insurance, voluntary tips, alcohol, additional drinks, and single occupancy are paid separately. These conditions also matter when comparing the [“Active Venezuela” itinerary](/venezuela/tour/active-venezuela-jurassic-water-world/), whose Puerto Ordaz–Canaima charter flight is an additional expense.

Match the prices of optional flights and trips with the final booking itinerary. The fact that an activity is possible within the park does not mean it is included in the basic six days.

## Choosing Between Short and Long Itineraries

Six days make sense when Canaima National Park and Angel Falls are your main goals, and free days provide flexibility. On [“New Conquistadors”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/), the journey instead continues to the Caribbean coast, Los Llanos, and the Andes, rather than spending extra time by one lagoon. That means more varied natural regions but significantly more travel.

“Colors of Venezuela” also suits travelers who want one genuinely active day at Angel Falls and otherwise prefer time in a hotel over a multi-day camping trek. It is not an entirely effortless journey: the boat and forest trail are included in the main itinerary.

## Frequently Asked Questions About “Colors of Venezuela”

### Are Caracas–Canaima–Caracas Flights Included?

Yes. Domestic flights on this route are included. International travel to Venezuela should be arranged separately.

### Is There a Fee to Enter Canaima?

Yes. The listing specifies a **$40 entrance fee**, payable locally, outside the included services.

### How Long Does the Angel Falls Excursion Last?

Most of day three, approximately from 05:00 to 18:00, is dedicated to the excursion. The route involves motorboats and a hike to the viewpoint.

### Is a Flight Over Angel Falls Guaranteed?

No. Aerial excursions are optional activities on days four and five, subject to separate arrangements and flying conditions. The main tour visits the waterfall by land and river.

### What Can I Do on the Two Free Days?

Relax beside the lagoon or choose one or more optional excursions. Listed flights, walks, and water activities have separate prices and arrangements; the program does not promise that all can fit into two days.

## How to Choose a Venezuela Itinerary

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. To narrow your options, first decide which experience is essential: [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), climbing [Mount Roraima](/venezuela/place/mount-roraima/), island relaxation, or discovering several natural regions. Then consider overnight accommodation and travel arrangements.

A trip using hotels, lodges, and seaside accommodation differs from a route with tents and hammocks, even when their overall duration is the same. Travel days matter too: flights, connections, and transfers to boats occupy time that cannot also be counted as a full sightseeing or beach day.

| Main Goal | Itinerary to Compare |
|---|---|
| Canaima without a long tour | [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/) |
| Waterfalls and the seaside | [“Best of Venezuela”](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) |
| Several natural regions | [“Natural Contrasts”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) |
| Multi-day mountain ascent | [Mount Roraima trekking](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-mount-roraima-trek-12-days/) |
| Caribbean and Bolivian Andes | [Venezuela and Bolivia](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/) |

The [Venezuela country guide](/venezuela/) covers regions and seasonal conditions. Here the purpose is different: comparing bookable itineraries and identifying what needs to be agreed for your chosen option.

## Short Canaima Tour: What Is Already Included?

[“Venezuelan Beauty: Canaima and Angel Falls”](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/) suits travelers concentrating on one natural area. The journey begins with a flight from [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/) and ends with a return to the same city. International arrival and subsequent travel are planned outside this short package.

Included are round-trip Caracas–Canaima airline tickets, lodge accommodation according to your chosen option, local transfers, guides and staff, a full-day excursion to Angel Falls, meals specified for each day, and kayaking. Visits to [Sapo](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/) and [Hacha](/venezuela/place/hacha-falls/) waterfalls are also included.

**The Angel Falls excursion and the free day serve different purposes.** On the excursion, travelers navigate rivers and hike to the waterfall. The free day is for relaxing at [Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/place/canaima-lagoon/); optional activities listed on the tour page are paid for separately. Listing them does not mean the entire selection is included.

Accommodation options are Tapuy Lodge and Waku Lodge. One day's description names Waku, so before paying, verify how the full itinerary applies to your selected lodge, room type, and meals. Also confirm guide languages and group size: the service list alone does not establish Russian-speaking guiding.

The national park entrance fee is excluded. Flight times on the tour page describe the intended itinerary, but actual schedules are confirmed at booking. When connecting to an international flight, calculate the full journey, not just the time of the return flight from Canaima.

## Angel Falls and Margarita: A Longer Relaxation Period

Choose [“Best of Venezuela” with Margarita Island](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) when you want to stay beside the sea after your nature excursions. The itinerary includes Caracas, Canaima, and [Margarita](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/). Its island section provides a consecutive block of free days with all-inclusive accommodation.

When comparing it to a more intensive nature tour, check **how many days have no mandatory transfers or excursions**. Here, beach relaxation is a distinct part of the holiday. An island sightseeing trip is optional, allowing you to keep your free time for resting.

There are also free days and choices of extra activities early in the Caracas section. The tour therefore does not imply an included excursion from morning to night every day. If you want each day planned in advance, agree separately on your activities and their cost.

Domestic flights, excursions, transfers, included meals, and a Russian-speaking guide are listed among the services. International flights, insurance, extra excursions, and the national park fee are excluded. Final confirmation should specify the language and amount of guiding at each stage.

All-inclusive service applies to accommodation on Margarita. It does not extend automatically to Caracas, Canaima, the entire holiday, or every drink on an excursion. For budgeting, review meals at each place you stay. Other seaside options appear among [Venezuela beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/venezuela/).

## Natural Contrasts: More Regions and More Accommodation Changes

[“Tropical Natural Contrasts”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) connects [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/), [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/), [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), the [Orinoco Delta](/venezuela/place/orinoco-delta/), and [Margarita](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/). Choose this journey for diversity if changing bases and taking domestic flights suits you.

Domestic flights and private transfers are included. Guiding differs by region, however: a Russian-speaking guide is specified in Caracas, English-speaking guides in Canaima and the Orinoco Delta, and hotel representatives at island stops. **Meeting a hotel representative and having an excursion guide are different services.**

Types of accommodation also change: hotels, a posada, and a campamento appear in the program. Before booking, match each stage with the specific accommodation and room arrangements. A city hotel's general category does not establish the same facilities at a nature camp.

Los Roques offers a short island section, while Margarita ends the trip with seaside relaxation. The Orinoco Delta adds boat travel through waterways and encounters with local nature. Check daily itineraries for the actual activities; wildlife watching never guarantees seeing a particular species.

Compare this tour with [“Best of Venezuela”](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) for intensity and rest time. ## Roraima: What Makes a Trekking Package Different?

The [Mount Roraima trekking tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-mount-roraima-trek-12-days/) involves several consecutive days on foot, climbing the plateau, exploring it, and descending. The journey then continues through [Puerto Ordaz](/venezuela/place/puerto-ordaz/) to [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). Travelers choose it for hiking, with wilderness overnight stays integral to the itinerary.

Accommodation includes hotels, a posada, campamento, tents, and hammocks. English-speaking guides are included, while Russian-speaking guiding costs extra. Porter service, a single-person tent, a mattress, and a sleeping bag are also listed as optional services or rentals. These details matter more when budgeting than the general word “active” in the tour's name.

Check every flight segment. Caracas–Puerto Ordaz and Canaima–Caracas are included. **The charter from Puerto Ordaz to Canaima is excluded from the base price**, even though it appears in the itinerary. Its cost and the number of participants require separate confirmation.

Do not choose this program only for a photograph of the summit or waterfall. You need to accept the whole travel style: long hikes, changing conditions, and camping. If those days are not your idea of a holiday, compare it with the [short Canaima itinerary](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/). Our [Venezuela adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/venezuela/) section describes active formats in greater detail.

## Venezuela and Bolivia: Accounting for Flights Between Countries

[“Venezuela and Bolivia: Nature and Culture”](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/) combines islands and waterfalls with Bolivia's highlands. The Venezuela section covers [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/), [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/), and [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), then the journey continues to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

Domestic flights within each country are included. Continental flights between Venezuela and Bolivia, like transatlantic airline tickets, are paid for separately. **A domestic flight and a flight between countries must not be combined under one vague heading of “flights included.”**

Russian-speaking guides are provided in Caracas and La Paz; other sections specify English-speaking guides and hotel representatives. Extended Russian-language guiding costs extra. If the guide's language matters for nature excursions, agree on it specifically for those days.

This combination makes sense for travelers wishing to discover both natural regions and willing to arrange extra international logistics. If the whole holiday should remain beside the Caribbean Sea, compare the [Margarita itinerary](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) first. ## What Should Be Confirmed Before You Travel?

| Item to Agree On | Details to Receive |
|---|---|
| Accommodation | Property and room type |
| Guiding | Language at each stage |
| Flights | Included and separate segments |
| Optional activities | Price and availability |
| Wilderness overnights | Equipment and facilities |
| Fees | Payments due locally |

On Venezuela itineraries, the current feasibility of each stage matters. Before paying, confirm domestic flights, ground transfers, access to nature programs, and local guiding contacts. Official international travel advisories warn of safety risks when visiting Venezuela and certain regions; take them into account when choosing destinations and reviewing insurance coverage.

River routes depend on weather and water levels. Listing an Angel Falls excursion means the journey is planned, while whether the route can actually operate on a particular day is confirmed locally. Check current entry and protected-area requirements for your citizenship and departure date; old references to health documents in itinerary descriptions do not replace this.

When asking us to help select a trip, tell us your main goal, travel dates, group size, preferred guiding language, and overnight accommodation preferences. For the short Canaima itinerary, include your plans before and after the tour to coordinate connections. For Roraima, discuss your hiking experience and equipment well in advance.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Choosing a Venezuela Tour

### Can I Visit Only Canaima, Without a Long Itinerary?

Yes. [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/) is a separate short program with round-trip flights from Caracas. International flights and the rest of the holiday are arranged separately.

### Which Tour Offers More Free Time by the Sea?

Start by comparing [“Best of Venezuela” with Margarita](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) with [“Natural Contrasts”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/). The first has a longer uninterrupted island stay; the second visits more regions and changes accommodation more often.

### Is a Russian-Speaking Guide Included on Every Tour?

No. On [“Natural Contrasts”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/), the Russian-speaking guide is listed in Caracas, while English-speaking guides work in the nature regions. On the [Roraima trek](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-mount-roraima-trek-12-days/), Russian-language guiding requires extra payment. Check the language at every stage.

### If a Flight Appears in the Itinerary, Is It Necessarily Paid For?

No. The [Roraima tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-mount-roraima-trek-12-days/) lists the Canaima charter separately. On the [Bolivia journey](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/), flights between countries are excluded. Compare flight segments against the included-services list.
